To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the proposed approach to discriminant analysis of EEG data can be used to differentiate patients with schizophrenia from healthy controls.

(1) LDF models with high sensitivity (over 90%) and specificity (over 80%) can be obtained using linear discriminant analysis; (2) the best LDF model was found to include 8 EEG parameters; (3) a formula for the best LDF was obtained and its generalizing ability was evaluated.

1) the proposed methodology for discriminant analysis of EEG allows to minimize the effect of overlearning and select the optimal LDF model; 2) the LDF obtained by the proposed methodology is able to discriminate patients with schizophrenia from healthy controls with 90% of sensitivity and 80 % of specificity; 3) the LDF model selected by the proposed methodology can be generalized to other EEG data sets.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a new approach to the diagnosis of schizophrenia using discriminant EEG analysis.
the problem of the EEG discriminant analysis for the diagnosis of schizophrenia.
the search of the best LDF for the EEG-based differential diagnosis of schizophrenia. 1
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
EEG discriminant analysis can be used for differential diagnosis of schizophrenia.
LDF models are not universal, they depend on EEG processing methods and the number of predictors.
the methodological approach proposed is a promising one and can be used for the development of the diagnostic and therapeutic algorithms for schizophrenia.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the proposed method allows obtaining a model that can be used for the differential diagnosis of schizophrenia.
the proposed methodology for EEG analysis allowed to obtain the LDF with the best diagnostic characteristics.
the EEG parameters of the standard EEG ranges theta (4-7 Hz), alpha (8-12 Hz) and beta (13-30 Hz) are the most significant in differentiating patients with schizophrenia from healthy individuals.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the LDF with a set of spectral and coherent parameters of the standard EEG ranges theta (3,5-7,5 Hz), alpha (7,5-12 Hz) and beta (12-30 Hz) is the most informative for differential diagnosis of schizophrenia.
the EEG discriminant analysis can be successfully used in differential diagnostics of schizophrenia.
the proposed method allows the development of a model with high sensitivity, high specificity and good generalizing ability.
